text:
Spike for question 2 done; the story stays open on product decisions. Tested in Chromium with real Vite 7.3.1 and Next.js 16.0.0, no routing changes, and React state in a counter.

1. Full reloads CAN be held from the injected script. A navigate listener calling preventDefault on navigationType reload stopped location.reload() on both, and stopped the reload Vite sends after an index.html edit. No platform method is patched. Limit: it cannot tell a dev server's reload from the application's own location.reload(), for example after logging out. Next.js did not attempt a reload for a layout edit.

2. Client HMR CANNOT be held from the injected script. It loads as a module at the end of body, after the HMR client has registered its listeners. Patching WebSocket.prototype.addEventListener at that point held nothing on either framework.

3. Client HMR CAN be held by a script that runs before the page's own. A WebSocket subclass buffered messages with stopImmediatePropagation, then re-dispatched them: both frameworks held the update, applied it on release, kept React state, and did not reload. This needs a classic script early in the document, and it wraps WebSocket, which the repository forbids (src/devtools/AGENTS.md: never patch host platform methods; features: never wrap WebSocket). Sockets: Vite on /, Next.js on /_next/webpack-hmr.

Not tested: holds longer than a few seconds (Next.js buffered 3 messages in 4 seconds, so heartbeats may be held too and a client could reconnect), server restarts, Firefox and Safari, SSE-based HMR, and Bun's HMR.

Decisions needed: (a) whether wrapping WebSocket is acceptable for this feature, or only full reloads get held; (b) whether intercepting an application's own location.reload() is acceptable, and what counts as using the page; (c) which frameworks come first; (d) what happens to Disable Reloads.
